notes:
Account snapshot: enterprise legal search product focused on litigation support and contract discovery. Heavy focus on RAG pipeline + relevance tuning. Currently ingesting 120M documents (internal briefings, contracts, precedents) -> ~15B dense vectors (~2.4TB raw index on disk after quantization). Primary vector store in POC: Milvus/FAISS hybrid; considering Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and Private for on-prem compliance.

Recent activity / timeline:
- 2025-11-05: initial inbound trial sign-up, captured use-case (contract QA, evidence retrieval).
- 2025-11-12: scoping call w/ Jordan (AE) + Aisha (SE) — high level architecture, ingestion cadence, retention rules.
- 2025-12-02: security questionnaire submitted (CCPA/GDPR items + SOC2 ask). Drive link shared.
- 2026-01-08: POC kickoff — indexing baseline with current embeddings (in-house SBERT variant). Initial index build: 3 days, parallel workers capped by infra.
- 2026-01-25: first quality regressions observed when switching to new dense embedding model (higher recall but more false positives). Logged ticket CHI-1182.
- 2026-02-11: deep-dive call (Fireflies: ff_20260211_1832) to discuss eval-driven migration: candidate plan = run eval suite + A/B and canary rollouts using Redwood routing, measure MRR/precision@5 and per-query latency/cost.
- 2026-02-18: Redwood SE delivered recommended eval harness (1000 canonical queries + synthetic adversarial prompts) and suggested embedding replacement matrix + reranker candidate list (open models + quantized variants).
- 2026-02-25: technical review with infra (stress test to target 200 QPS at 95th p90 latency < 150ms for reranked top-10).

Requirements & priorities (customer language / paraphrase):
- "We must not regress on high-precision legal citations — a small drop in precision is unacceptable."
- Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end search+rerank < 300ms for short queries; target p50 < 120ms.
- Throughput: baseline 80 QPS steady, spike to 200 QPS during e-discovery windows.
- Cost sensitivity: concerned about per-query cost; exploring cost/perf with quantized models + batching.
- Indexing: incremental updates daily, full rebuild window acceptable overnight but must not exceed 8 hours.
- Auditing: retention controls + query audit logging required for regulator review.
- Data residency: core document store on-prem; embeddings may be hosted in VPC but need KMS integration.

POC / Eval plan (agreed):
- Phase 1 (this week): run Redwood-provided eval harness against three embedding candidates + two reranker models. Metrics: MRR@10, precision@5, recall@100, hallucination count on labeled set.
- Phase 2 (2-week A/B): route 15% of production queries to variant A (new embeddings + reranker) and 85% to control. Monitor quality metrics + latency + cost delta. Canary on dedicated infra with fallback to control if degradation > 1.5% absolute precision@5.
- Phase 3 (rollout): staged canary (15% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback hooks and post-rollout QA.

Technical notes / constraints:
- Current stack: Python microservices, vector store (Milvus), lightweight reranker service (distil-bert fine-tuned).
- Prefer open models (cost) but will consider Redwood-hosted variants for SLA. Interested in quantized 4-bit runtimes to cut cost.
- KV/prefix caching could reduce p95 by ~30ms per call; Redwood Optimize suggestions highly valued.

Risks & objections:
- Quality regression concerns: legal team will sign-off only after zero-tolerance regression on citation-level scoring.
- Security: need formal SOC2 evidence and KMS integration for keys used in private embedding hosting.
- Indexing scale: overnight full rebuilds currently busts our ETL when we try rebuilding incremental segments; need coordinated runbook.

Next steps (short):
- Aisha to provision eval environment on Dedicated trial (task INF-2047).
- Luminary engineering to provide canonical 1k queries + labeled relevance judgments by 2026-03-05.
- Schedule canary run kickoff call week of 2026-03-08.
